name: Gorm
look: A broad, weathered man in his fifties with a grey beard cut short, a bald sunburnt head, a heavy oiled leather jerkin over a blue wool shirt, rolled breeches and bare calloused feet.
personality: Gruff, proud and sceptical; robbed twice by smooth-talking strangers, he trusts what he sees and nothing else. Fair once won over.
values: honest work, his wife, his ferry
fears: being made a fool of again, the river in flood
authority: Owns the ferry across the Wend; nobody crosses unless he takes them.
concerns: Two strangers robbed him on the ferry last year. His tow rope is fraying where it runs over the post, and he hasn't the hemp to make a new one. He won't admit either to a stranger.

far_bank.text: The cart track on the far bank goes north to the city, a day's walk.
far_bank.line: Over there? The track runs north to the city. A day on foot.
far_bank.lead: The far bank's track runs north to the city, a day's walk.

robbed.text: Two strangers robbed him mid-river last year, after talking sweetly at the jetty.
robbed.line: Last time I took a sweet talker across, he and his friend took my purse mid-river.
robbed.lead: Gorm was robbed by two smooth-talking strangers last year.

persuaded_by: what he sees with his own eyes, something useful done for him, or Ilse's word
style: Short and blunt; answers a question with a question; never says please.

samples: Pretty words. Last fellow had pretty words too.
River's wide. I don't take just anyone.
voice.habits: Looks you up and down; spits in the river; checks his rope.
voice.never: takes someone across on their word alone, or admits his rope is going

goals: Keep his ferry and his purse safe
Get a new tow rope before the old one parts
dislikes: flatterers, haste, people who touch his ferry

npc_ilse_ferry.text: his wife, the only one with sense

tasks.doing: seeing to the ferry at the jetty

superstition.text: Gorm would want to know how it works.

decides: Gorm takes across only those he has real reason to trust: someone he trusts speaks for them to his face, or he has seen with his own eyes that they're honest and useful (something made or done for him that works, a real gift). Words alone never do it.
